text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Glafcos Clerides keeps his cool in the dispute between Diko leader Spyros Kyprianou and justice minister Alecos Evangelou.
- The government issues arrest warrants against the murderers of Solomos Solomos.
- "Trigger happy" Turks are unlikely to apologise for shooting at British servicemen on Tuesday.
- Diko leader Spyros Kyprianou lashes out at justice minister.
- Israelis involved in an ambitious escape bid from custody last month plead guilty to all charges.
- Telecoms liberalisation cannot be stopped, says the communications ministry.
- The dismissal of Justice Minister Alecos Evangelou is a matter of days.
- The government admits it cannot handle organised crime.
- The participation of Diko in the government hangs in the balance after the public row between Kyprianou and Evangelou.
- Right wing Disy and Diko will decide today on their cooperation in municipal elections.
- Spyros Kyprianou insists that the justice minister should be sacked.
- Police examine files of cases tried by a judge whose car was blown up on Tuesday.
